topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the core learning outcomes of the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: intrinsic mutations, environmental exposures, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce how cancer develops through genetic mutations and microenvironmental factors, evaluating the relative contributions of stochastic internal processes versus environmental exposures across populations.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how pathogens drive malignant transformation through direct cellular disruption, chronic inflammation, and immune modulation, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental agents and metabolic processes induce DNA damage through reactive adducts, thymine dimers, and oxidative stress across different tissues.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and carcinogenesis mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish non-mutagenic tumor promoters and developmental windows of host susceptibility from initiators in driving carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and assessing exposure risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail genomic, epidemiological, and experimental approaches for detecting carcinogenicity and evaluating cancer risks against societal benefits.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and final summary of the lecture.
